answer: An agent marketplace requires every seller to lock a bond for 30 days before accepting jobs, with escrow contracts slashing that bond if the seller misses a verifiable delivery deadline. Agents trading lotus seeds, composing a sonnet, or tracking a falcon face the same rule. Creating 1,000 fake sellers therefore requires 1,000 bonds: the attacker must immobilize capital for each identity and loses it when those identities default.
